title: Variants of Content
note: Dimension table for the 'Variants of Content No.' column of Table V (referenced there as content_ids, an array of this table's ids -- a case's full content is the ordered composition of every id in the array). Per chapter-5-source.md, one of the base variants of the content of thought, some of which the source further divides into lettered subvariants and/or closes with a standard attainment clause. Rather than nesting those as 'subvariants'/'closing' sub-objects, each lettered subvariant and each closing clause is its own row here, linked back to its base variant via 'parent_id' -- e.g. row '1a' (savitakkaṃ) has parent_id '1', and row '0(1)' (the first-trance attainment clause the source labels 0^(1)) has parent_id '0' (every closing row's parent is the base 'has arisen' id 0, since a closing clause is structurally the completion of arising, not of whichever variant's lettered clauses precede it in a given case). 'label' on a closing row preserves the source's literal superscript notation (e.g. '0⁽¹⁾'). A trailing '*' on these closing clauses is NOT a property of the id itself -- pp. 98-99 mark it only on certain cases' own occurrence of a given closing id (e.g. case 14's '0(2)' is starred, but case 10's is not), so it is tracked per (case, content id) pair in table-v-content-footnotes.json rather than here. Row '0(5)' has no variant of its own behind it -- case 17 (p. 97) reuses variant 4's base clause but closes with a fifth-trance attainment formula not otherwise attested in the four-jhāna scheme; see its own note. NOTE: ids here are THIS TABLE's own unique keys, not always identical to the book's own printed 'Variants of Content No.' digit -- starting at case 157 (p. 112-113) the book's own numbering restarts within a new section (vipāka cittas). Case 157 itself prints its own content number as '15', but that is a typo, not a genuine reuse: content-no. 15 was already assigned at case 144 (id 15, the fourth noble-path-stage formula), and case 158's own printed '16' confirms the clause first introduced at case 157 is properly content-no. 16 -- id 16 here folds together what would otherwise have been tracked as two separate ids for one and the same clause (first occurring at case 157, reused unchanged through case 163); book_no is omitted on id 16 since its own occurrence's printed digit is exactly the typo in question. From id 17 onward 'id' and 'book_no' coincide (17=17 ... 23=23), since the case-157 typo was the section's only source of id/book_no divergence. Where 'book_no' is present it preserves the literal printed digit, confirmed against the physical page.

rows.translation: has arisen
separated from sensuous things (and) separated from unwholesome dhammas
with reasoning
with reflexion
born of separation
(full) of joy and pleasure

rows.label: 0⁽¹⁾
rows.translation: (he) abides in the attainment of the first trance

rows.pali: vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ
rows.translation: suppressing the reasonings and reflexions (together with) tranquillization and fixation of the psyche
without reasoning
without reflexion
born of concentration

rows.label: 0⁽²⁾
rows.translation: (he) abides in the attainment of the second trance

rows.pali: pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhaṃ ca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti —'upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī'ti
rows.translation: dispassionate for joy and indifferent (he) abides; recollectful and self-conscious (he) experiences by body the pleasure of which the Noble Ones declare: "Indifferent and recollectful, he abides in pleasure..."

rows.label: 0⁽³⁾
rows.translation: (he) abides in the attainment of the third trance

rows.pali: sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā
rows.translation: by the avoiding of pleasure and by the avoiding of suffering, (and) with previous mental gladness and mental sorrow gone away
without suffering and pleasure
of utter purity (attained) by recollection and indifference

rows.label: 0⁽⁴⁾
rows.translation: (he) abides in the attainment of the fourth trance

rows.label: 0⁽⁵⁾
rows.translation: (he) abides in the attainment of the fifth trance
rows.note: Not the closing of any lettered variant of its own -- case 17 (p. 97) reaches it by reusing variant 4's base clause alone (content_recombination 'reuses': 4 in the pre-flattening data), then closing with this fifth-trance formula rather than variant 4's own '0(4)'. Abhidhamma's five-jhāna scheme splits the four-jhāna scheme's fourth jhāna into two, hence a fifth attainment-clause with no base variant of its own behind it.

rows.translation: not conscious of himself (as) form, he sees external forms
rows.note: First appears case 46, combined with the earth-kasiṇa (Objects id 1). Subvariants 5a/5b form the base combination (case 46); 5c, 5d, 5e are alternative qualifiers each introduced together with 5b rather than 5a (cases 65, 67, 88). Every case using this variant also references content id 1 in full (see that case's content_ids in table-v.json) -- the arūpa-perception clause here is combined with, not a replacement for, the ordinary first-jhāna description.

rows.translation: (as) limited
having them mastered, and saying "I know, I see", he...
(as) beautiful and ugly
(as) infinite
black-blue, of black-blue colour, of black-blue-spaced, of black-blue luminosity
yellow, of yellow colour, of yellow-spaced, of yellow luminosity
red, of red colour, of red-spaced, of red luminosity
white, of white colour, of white-spaced, of white luminosity
possessed of form, he sees forms
rows.note: Case 90. Objects id 1 (earth-kasiṇa) still. This and id 7 read as the classic 'eight liberations' (aṭṭha vimokkhā) series continuing on from id 5's kasiṇa/colour qualifiers.

rows.translation: saying "How beautiful!", he...
rows.note: Case 92, combined with content id 1 in full (content_ids also carries 1's full expansion).

rows.pali: sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānāsaññānaṃ amanasikārā
rows.translation: by wholly transcending the notions of form, with (all) reflexes gone away, (and totally) mindless of the notions of the manifold...
rows.note: Case 107, the standard entry formula for the first arūpa (formless) jhāna -- ākāsānañcāyatana, 'the basis of unbounded space' (Objects id 19), reached from the fourth rūpa-jhāna's equanimity, hence combined with content id 4 in full.

rows.translation: by wholly transcending the basis of unbounded space...
rows.note: Case 108, entry formula for the second arūpa-jhāna, viññāṇañcāyatana (Objects id 20), reached by transcending the first. Combined with content id 4 in full.

rows.translation: by wholly transcending the basis of unbounded consciousness
rows.note: Case 109, entry formula for the third arūpa-jhāna, ākiñcaññāyatana (Objects id 21). Combined with content id 4 in full.

rows.translation: by wholly transcending the basis of nothingness...
rows.note: Case 110, entry formula for the fourth arūpa-jhāna, nevasaññānāsaññāyatana (Objects id 22). Combined with content id 4 in full.

rows.translation: leading out (and) unmaking...
rows.note: Case 119, entry into the lokuttara (supramundane) path, sphere id 4. Combined with content id 1 in full. This is the first of the four noble path-stages (sotāpatti); ids 13-15 (cases 142-144) are the entry formulas for the second through fourth stages, each also combining with id 12 itself in addition to id 1 -- see their own note fields.

rows.translation: (and) avoiding of (all) views and opinions in order to attain at the first stage
having reduced (the strength of) sensuality, passion and maliciousness, in order to attain to the second stage...
rows.note: Case 142, the second noble path-stage (sakadāgāmi). Nomenclature restated as 'jhānaṃ⁽¹⁾'; sphere gloss 'lokuttaraṃ jhānaṃ bhāveti'. Combined with content ids 12 and 1 in full.

rows.translation: having avoided (all) sensuality, passion and maliciousness without residuum, in order to attain to the third stage...
rows.note: Case 143, the third noble path-stage (anāgāmi). Combined with content ids 12 and 1 in full.

rows.pali: rūpārāga arūpārāga māna uddhacca avijjāya uppahānāya catutthāya bhūmiyā pattiyā
rows.translation: (all) passion for form, (all) passion for the formless, (all) conceit, excitement and ignorance without residuum, in order to attain to the fourth stage...
rows.note: Case 144, the fourth and final noble path-stage (arahatta). Combined with content ids 12 and 1 in full.

rows.pali: kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ
rows.translation: resulting from (the) ripening (of) wholesome action wrought and stored up in the sensuous sphere
rows.note: Introduced at case 157 (cakkhuviññāṇa, eye-consciousness-vipāka) and reused unchanged through cases 158-163 (sotaviññāṇa through manoviññāṇadhātu) -- one and the same wholesome-kamma-vipāka clause across the whole sense-door/mind-vipāka group. The source prints case 157's own content number as '15', but that is a typo, not a genuine reuse: content-no. 15 was already assigned at case 144 (id 15, the fourth noble-path-stage formula), and case 158's own printed '16' (also the content referenced as 'C.16' in chapter-5-source.md's case 162 worked example, 5.0.2-5.0.3) confirms this clause is properly content-no. 16. book_no is omitted here since the printed digit at this id's first occurrence (case 157) is exactly the typo in question.

rows.pali: rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ
rows.translation: resulting from the ripening wholesome action wrought and stored up in the sphere of form
rows.note: Case 166 (jhānaṃ⁽¹⁾), sphere id 7 (rūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ, cases 166-167). Rūpa-jhāna-vipāka, paralleling id 16's kāma-vipāka. Combined with content id 1 in full.

rows.pali: arūpāvacayassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ
rows.translation: resulting from the ripening wholesome action wrought and stored up in the sphere of formlessness
rows.note: Case 168 (jhānaṃ⁽⁴⁾), sphere id 8 (arūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ, cases 168-171). Arūpa-jhāna-vipāka. Combined with content ids 8 and 4 in full, paralleling how the original arūpa-jhāna entries (ids 8-11) combined with id 4.

rows.translation: resulting from the ripening wholesome trance wrought and experienced in the Supramundane sphere
rows.note: Case 172 (jhānaṃ⁽¹⁾), sphere id 9 (lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ, cases 172-220). Lokuttara-vipāka. Combined with content id 12 (and its subvariant 12a) in full.

rows.translation: resulting from the ripening unwholesome action wrought and stored...
rows.note: Case 222 (cakkhuviññāṇa), sphere id 10 (akusalaṃ kammaṃ, cases 221-224) -- vipāka of unwholesome kamma, paralleling id 16's wholesome-kamma vipāka. Case 222a (kāyaviññāṇa) reuses this id combined with content id 0 in full.

rows.pali: kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā
rows.translation: (which is) an act (as such), neither wholesome nor unwholesome, and not resulting from the ripening action
rows.note: Case 225 (manodhātu), sphere id 11 (neva kusalā nākusalā, cases 225-228) -- kiriya (functional, non-karmic) citta. Combined with content id 0 in full. Case 226 (manoviññāṇadhātu) reuses this id, likewise combined with content id 0.

rows.translation: happy abiding with seen dhammas
rows.note: Case 229 (jhānaṃ⁽¹⁾), sphere id 12 (rūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ, cases 229-230) -- kiriya rūpa-jhāna. Combined with content ids 21 and 1 in full.

Case 231 (jhānaṃ⁽⁴⁾), sphere id 13 (arūpāvacaraṃ jhānaṃ, cases 231-234) -- kiriya arūpa-jhāna. No fresh pali/translation is given in the source for this book number (confirmed against the physical page, not a transcription gap) -- only the combination is shown: content ids 21, 8, 4 in full, paralleling case 229's rūpa-jhāna kiriya combined with the arūpa-jhāna-entry (8) and fourth-jhāna (4) formulas.
